statement_record.book: An adjunction consists of F : C -> D, U : D -> C and eta : 1_C => U o F such that for every C, D and every f : C -> U(D) there is a unique g : F(C) -> D with f = U(g) o eta_C. F is the left adjoint, U the right adjoint, eta the unit; written F -| U.
statement_record.intree: universal_arrow_from_UMP takes exactly this data pointwise — an object d, a morphism η : c ~> F d, and (∀ d' f, ∃! g, f ≈ fmap[F] g ∘ η) — and AdjunctionFromUniversalArrows turns a family of such into a genuine Adjunction (F ⊣ U notation of Theory/Adjunction.v).
statement_record.strength_comparison: same. Presentation differs: the in-tree unit is given pointwise (one universal arrow per object of C) and its naturality as Id ⟹ U ◯ F is derived rather than assumed — a weaker hypothesis for the same conclusion. The left adjoint is reconstructed as LeftAdjointFunctorFromUniversalArrows rather than taken as given, so for a pre-existing F the conclusion arrives up to natural isomorphism (left_adjoint_iso); no mathematical content of the definition is lost. Terminology (left/right adjoint, unit, F ⊣ U) is fixed in Theory/Adjunction.v.
